title: Connected subgroup quotients of a finite etale torsor with geometric fibre cardinality
statement: Let $U$ be a nonempty connected scheme [def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $Q$ a finite group in its universe, $c:Y\to U$ a connected finite etale $\operatorname{ULift}(Q)$-torsor [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois], and $H\le Q$ any subgroup. There exist a connected finite etale $v:V\to U$, a connected finite etale $\operatorname{ULift}(H)$-torsor $c_H:Y_H\to V$, and an isomorphism $e:Y_H\simeq Y$ such that $c\circ e=v\circ c_H$. For every separably closed field $\Omega$ in the universe of $U$ and every $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$, the geometric fibre of $v$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-fibre] has cardinality $[Q:H]$. This statement involves no prime, module sheaf, representation, or associated-sheaf functor.

source.place: Tag 0A3R, proof at T = Y/H; pione.tex Tag 0BND (1)-(3), Section 03SF; finite etale fibres over separably closed fields

proof.text: Restrict the deck action to H and regard it as a SingleObj H diagram of finite etale U-schemes. Take its quotient cocone, using the finite-group quotient and exact geometric fibre functor of lem-fet-galois-category. In Lean this is Scheme.FiniteEtale.quotientCocone; fiber_quotientCocone says that its leg p is surjective on a geometric fibre and identifies precisely H-orbits. The quotient structure map v is finite etale, as are morphisms between finite etale U-schemes. The conservative fibre functor implies that p is surjective (surjective_of_surjective_fiber). Hence V is connected as the continuous surjective image of the connected scheme c.P.

The quotient cocone is H-invariant. Two points of c.P over a geometric point of V have equal quotient images, so the quotient-fibre orbit relation gives an h in H carrying one to the other. Its equivalence closure is already the orbit relation: use 1 for reflexivity, inverse for symmetry, and multiplication for transitivity. Uniqueness follows directly from the original Q-torsor isomorphism: equality after acting by g and h gives equality of the two inclusions into the disjoint coproduct, forcing g=h. Thus H acts simply transitively on this fibre. The conservative finite etale fibre functor gives the H-torsor isomorphism (isIso_sigmaDesc_of_existsUnique). Construct cH using c.P itself, the map p, and the restricted action. Its connectedness is the original instance on c.P, and e is the identity. Cocone compatibility is p followed by v equals c.π.

For any finite torsor under a group G and any separably closed geometric point s, its geometric fibre has cardinality Nat.card G. Indeed the surjectivity and split finite etale fibre of lem-galois-geometric-fibre give a lift a of s. The map g to a followed by the action of g is injective by disjointness of coproduct summands. It is surjective because the pair (b,a) lifts through the torsor isomorphism, and a morphism from Spec of a field to a coproduct factors through a unique summand. This argument applies to both c and cH and to every separably closed field in the given universe.

For each s, identify the fibre of p followed by v with the dependent sum over b in the fibre of v of the fibre of p over b. Since each latter fibre has cardinality Nat.card H, finite dependent-sum counting gives Nat.card Q = Nat.card(v.GeometricFiber s) * Nat.card H. Mathlib Subgroup.index_mul_card gives Nat.card Q = H.index * Nat.card H. Cancel the positive natural number Nat.card H. ULift does not change cardinality. This includes H=1, H=Q, and Q=1 without excluding rank one.

theorem Scheme.GaloisCover.exists_connected_subgroup_quotient
    {U : Scheme.{u}} [ConnectedSpace U]
    (Q : Type u) [Group Q] [Finite Q]
    (c : Scheme.GaloisCover (ULift.{u + 1} Q) U) [ConnectedSpace c.P]
    (H : Subgroup Q) :
    ∃ (V : Scheme.{u}) (v : V ⟶ U) (_ : IsFinite v) (_ : Etale v)
      (_ : ConnectedSpace V),
      (∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsSepClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ U),
        Nat.card (v.GeometricFiber s) = H.index) ∧
      ∃ (cH : Scheme.GaloisCover (ULift.{u + 1} H) V) (_ : ConnectedSpace cH.P)
        (e : cH.P ≅ c.P), e.hom ≫ c.π = cH.π ≫ v
